Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along the line segment from the point $(-2,3)$ to the point $(0,0),$ as shown above?

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=⟨2t-2,\,3-3t⟩.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a line segment with endpoints $(-2,3)$ and $(0,0).$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(-2+t(0-(-2))),\,(3+t(0-3))⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-2,\,3-3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(2t-2)^{2}(3-3t) \\  & =4(t-1)^{2}\cdot 3(1-t) \\  & =-12(t-1)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-12(t-1)^{3}\cdot 2\,\text{d}t \\  & =-24{\int }_{0}^{1}(t-1)^{3}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
